title.narrative: Enhancing GBV services in Kombolcha Town, Kalu Woredas, Debre Birhan and Dessie, Amhara Region through Capacity building, community awareness raising and strengthening WLOs

description.narrative: ltpgtConflicts have devastating consequences. Women have fewer resources to protect themselves and their children, the majority of displaced people are women and girls, and they become targets of violence. Due to the recent conflict, instability, and lack of peace and security in the intervention area many women, girls and even some boys have experienced conflict-related sexual violence, and ongoing new forms of GBV but due to the fragility of the security situation, women were not able to seek help therefore some work still needs to be done to support women to report cases of violence and get support.ltbrgtThis project addresses the lack of services for women and girl survivors in Amhara, Kombolcha Town, Kalu Woredas, Debre Birhan and Dessie by providing holistic and inclusive support that includes:ltbrgt1. Preparing awareness creation campaigns and conducting outreach service provisions, particularly to support IDP communities.ltbrgt2. Capacity building for relevant government actors, such as One Stop Centers, enhancing nutritional and health services provision within the existing safe houses in the Amhara region (Kombolcha, Dessie and Debre Birhan safe houses), the Bureau of Women Social Affairs, the Woreda bureau of Health, the bureau of Justice, police commissions, and Woreda-level officials, helping them understand concepts like GBV, CRSV, PSEA/safeguarding concerns, and a survivor-centered approach.ltbrgtAdditionally, the project focuses on enhancing emergency response capacity of Women-Led Organizations (WLOs) in Debre Birhan, Dessie, Kombolcha and Kalu regarding case management capacities, psychological counseling and developing an integrated capacity-building plan on GBV and Child Protection, referrals for specialized medical and psychological care. It also aims to provide legal services and support to victims of SGBV and CRSV, refer allegations to relevant organizations, and incorporate mentoring and training on PSEA/safeguarding while building the capacity of the existing Mobile Health and Nutrition Teams (MHNT) to enhance GBV identification and multisectoral response approach.lt/pgtltpgtThe project supports 7665 targeted individuals through different modalities.ltbrgtlt/pgt
